elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: § 23.4 as rendered grants the licence "to Customer and, upon written notice to M&I, its Affiliates"; note also that "Customer" is defined as Tri City National Bank "including its Affiliates".

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: § 23.4 names only Customer and its Affiliates; no reference to contractors acting on Customer's behalf, and § 23.5 confines use to "Customer's own internal processing and computing needs" (the only third-party reference is "Customer (or its designee)" in the use covenant, not the grant).
The grant remains "through the end of the Term" notwithstanding "payment of the then current license fees"; no perpetual term was inserted.
No "irrevocable" language added; the licence is term-limited and conditioned on release events under Article 23.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: Nothing in the rendered § 23.4/§ 23.5 limits termination of the licence to uncured material breach; the licence simply expires at end of Term.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Transferability is limited to "Customer's successor in a merger or acquisition transaction"; a general successor transfer right (e.g. asset sale, reorganisation) is not granted, and § 23.5(1) still bars transfer except "as permitted by Section 23.4".

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: § 23.4: "M&I hereby grants to Customer and, upon written notice to M&I, its Affiliates a non-exclusive license" — coverage keyed exactly to written notice.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: "non-transferable" deleted and replaced by "transferable to Customer's successor in a merger or acquisition transaction"; the conforming edit to § 23.5(1) ("to any third party other than as permitted by Section 23.4") removes the otherwise contradictory no-transfer covenant.

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: both fallback elements appear in operative language of § 23.4, and the § 23.5(1) covenant was conformed so no retained sentence contradicts the new transfer right.

Preferred level fails on four elements — contractors acting on Customer's behalf are not added to the grant; the licence is still "through the end of the Term" rather than perpetual and irrevocable on payment of the then-current fees; no breach-only termination limit; and transferability is narrowed to an M&A successor rather than Customer's successors generally. To reach preferred the drafter must (i) insert "and its contractors acting on its behalf" in the grant and conform § 23.5's "solely for Customer's own internal processing" clause, (ii) state that upon payment of the licence fees the licence is perpetual and irrevocable, (iii) add that the licence may be terminated only for Customer's uncured material breach, and (iv) broaden the transfer right to "Customer's successors".

Minimality holds: the only deletion is "non-transferable" (inside the targeted element), the two insertions map one-to-one to the fallback elements, and the eight-word § 23.5(1) carve-back is a necessary conforming edit rather than an extra requirement. No survival tails, expense language, procedures or unrelated boilerplate were added.

Intent preserved: the Term limitation, release-event conditions, licence-fee payment condition, internal-use and field-of-use restrictions in § 23.5(2)-(3), and the § 22.4 assignment mechanics all survive without contradiction, and the cross-reference to Section 23.4 is live.

Observation (not a failure): because "Customer" is defined to include its Affiliates, the affiliate coverage may already exist without notice; the added "upon written notice to M&I" language is therefore arguably duplicative and imposes a condition on coverage we may already hold. If pressed, consider "which grant extends to Customer's Affiliates" without the notice trigger, or a "for the avoidance of doubt" formulation, so the edit cannot be read as narrowing the existing definition.
